rationale: C13 is explicitly identified by the child as the prior disapproval establishing the controlling principle, and it supplies both the substantive rationale and the drafting structure: describe the wrongful death, identify existing survivor benefits, characterize the general benefits system as comprehensive, and reject a supplemental private award as inconsistent with that system. C25 and C23 contain closely related machinery and language, but C13 is the direct and expressly acknowledged template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: This principle had led to the disapproval of other private bills granting special awards in such cases (see H.R. 1315, 85th Congress, "A bill for the relief of Mr. and Mrs. Charles H. Page," disapproved on September 7, 1957).
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I HAVE WITHHELD my approval from H. R. 1315, a bill "For the relief of Mr. and Mrs. Charles H. Page."
shared_material.explanation: The child expressly cites C13 by bill number, title, and disapproval date as the precedent governing the present case.

shared_material.child_excerpt: there is a generous, comprehensive, and assured system of benefits provided for the survivors of veterans who die, in whatever manner, as a result of hospitalization by the VA
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Federal Government has provided a costly, comprehensive and orderly system of benefits for survivors of members of the Armed Forces who die in service. As long as the death is service-connected, these benefits are payable regardless of the cause
shared_material.explanation: Both use a distinctive comprehensive-benefits-system rationale and stress that benefits apply regardless of how the service-connected death occurred.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I firmly believe that the assured and general benefits to which survivors are entitled by law should be their exclusive remedy.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: H. R. 1315 would add to the benefits, to which the parents have heretofore or may hereafter become entitled, a further award
shared_material.explanation: The child adapts C13's rejection of a private award added to generally available survivor benefits into an explicit exclusive-remedy formulation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I perceive no basis for reaching a different result under the analogous circumstances of the present case.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: To make such an award in this case would establish a most undesirable precedent with respect to other cases involving service-connected deaths.
shared_material.explanation: The child's conclusion treats its facts as analogous to C13 and carries forward C13's rule against supplemental awards in service-connected-death cases.
